source: RMC-BestFit/src/RMC.BestFit/Estimation/GeneralizedMethodOfMoments.cs (the delegate constructor, C# 143, and the three delegates it takes) @ c2e6192
reference: RMC.BestFit @ c2e6192. Runs corehydro::numerics::support::run_callback (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback_runner.hpp), group "gmm", method "fit", against the delegates named by `construct.callback` (the moment conditions), `construct.jacobian` and `construct.penalty` -- each a function the four runners write themselves as a native closure (a C++ lambda, an R closure, a Python function, a C# delegate), so every case crosses the real host-language boundary. This is upstream's OWN API: GeneralizedMethodOfMoments has TWO constructors, one taking an IGMMModel (C# 106) and one taking these delegates directly (C# 143), and `IGMMModel` has exactly one implementation -- Bulletin17CDistribution -- so until this group existed the packages could fit an LP3 flood-frequency model by GMM and nothing else. EVERY expected value here is EMITTER-READ: no upstream test fits this model, so the oracle is the real RMC.BestFit GeneralizedMethodOfMoments driven by tools/oracle_emitter with the equivalent C# delegates, never a value computed by this repo's own C++. Every catalog callback is built from + - * / alone, with each summation written as an explicit loop rather than any language's sum(), mean() or Average(): R's sum() and mean() accumulate in extended precision where C++, Python and C# accumulate in double, and one differing bit moves a fitted parameter. THE MODEL is the just-identified two-parameter method-of-moments fit of a Normal -- theta = (mu, sigma2), g = [mean(x - mu), mean((x - mu)^2 - sigma2)] -- chosen because its GMM optimum has a CLOSED FORM: q = p makes g(theta-hat) = 0 attainable, and the unique root is the sample mean (4.95) and the population variance (0.165) of the eight observations. So the parameter assertions are checkable arithmetic, not a regression against whatever the optimizer happened to return. j_stat is NOT asserted anywhere in this file, deliberately: on a just-identified fit the moment residual covariance V = S - D(D'S^-1 D)^-1 D' is THEORETICALLY ZERO, so g' V^-1 g is whatever inverting a numerically singular matrix happens to give. Measured on this exact problem across the four optimizers -- all converging to the same parameters to 1e-9 -- it is -1.3e-09, 8.6e+19, -7.7e-15 and 0.126, and under NelderMead it THROWS outright from R and Python (where callback/gmm.hpp reports NaN rather than failing an otherwise exact fit) while returning a number from the C++ fixture runner, whose compiled callback contracts `a * a - theta` into an FMA. fixtures/estimation/gmm_bulletin17c_smoke.json's |J| < 1e-3 check holds only because its far messier real-data V carries real noise; on this deliberately clean synthetic problem any bound would be a fiction. j_stat_pval is NaN because the degrees of freedom q - p = 0: a just-identified fit has no over-identifying restriction left over to test its own specification with. That is correct, not a defect (see docs/upstream-csharp-issues.md). Tolerances follow fixtures/README.md's policy: optimizer-dependent parameters rel 1e-8, finite-difference-sensitive standard_error/covariance/correlation rel 1e-7. The result layout (parameter[j] / standard_error[j] / covariance[i,j] / correlation[i,j] / the J-statistic and bookkeeping scalars, dims = {p, p}) is documented in core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback/gmm.hpp; the `named` assertions below read it by label rather than by an index that shifts with the parameter count.

callbacks.Mom_NormalMeanVariance: moment_conditions(parameters) -> (g, s) with g = [mean(x - mu), mean((x - mu)^2 - sigma2)] and s = the 2 x 2 covariance of those two contributions, over x = [4.1, 5.2, 4.8, 5.5, 4.9, 5.1, 5.3, 4.7]; every sum an explicit loop  [corehydro addition, upstream's `(Vector G, Matrix S) MomentConditionFunction(double[])` shape: the textbook just-identified method-of-moments fit of a Normal, whose root is the sample mean and the population variance]
callbacks.Jac_NormalMeanVariance: jacobian(parameters) -> the analytic 2 x 2 dg/dtheta of Mom_NormalMeanVariance, one ROW per moment condition: [[-1, 0], [-2 mean(x - mu), -1]]  [corehydro addition, upstream's `double[,] JacobianFunction(double[])` shape: replaces the ported bounds-aware finite-difference Jacobian, so this case pins the analytic path rather than the numerical one]
callbacks.Pen_SigmaTowardsOne: penalty(parameters) -> 0.5 * (sigma2 - 1)^2  [corehydro addition, upstream's `double PenaltyFunction(double[])` shape: a ridge penalty carrying its own 1/2, as the half-quadratic convention in Q() expects. It pulls sigma2 away from the closed-form 0.165 and towards 1, which is what makes this case an oracle for the delegate being reached at all rather than a repeat of the first]
